name: Use the canonical catalog language from the context documents
description: The domain terms live in CONTEXT-MAP.md (the contexts and how they relate) and docs/contexts/<context>/CONTEXT.md (one glossary per context). Catalog and Inventory are written; others are added when their first seed starts. Use these terms exactly in code, docs and the UI, and check the glossary before adding a term. Keep the files current with the domain-modeling skill (~/.agents/skills/domain-modeling): a CONTEXT.md is only a glossary, with 1–2 sentence definitions and an Avoid list. docs/PRODUCT_PLAN.md was never committed and is unavailable.

title: Save every change to part details as a new, complete revision
rationale: Each change to part details saves a new, complete revision that never changes afterwards, grouped in a Change with a reason. Commands carry the current revision they expect. Restoring adds a new revision, and a change that alters nothing is rejected. (Restore itself was removed in kicad-parts-9296; mx-5e5fb1 replaces this decision when kicad-parts-7556 lands.) Supplier data, stock, scans and drafts never create revisions.

title: Keep a CAD item's identity, its stored bytes and its revisions separate
rationale: A CAD item keeps its identity over time. Its stored bytes are identified by their SHA-256, and each revision's hash covers its content and license. Source and license belong to one exact CAD item revision. Moving or copying stored bytes never creates a revision.

title: Keep verification and protection separate
rationale: Verification is permanent proof about one exact revision. Protection is an audited setting that blocks changes to a part or CAD item. To fix a protected item, remove the protection with a reason, revise it, verify the new revision, then protect it again. Authority is never a silent way around protection.

name: Binary-safe content addressing inside PocketBase hooks
description: $security.sha256 hashes text, so bytes that are not UTF-8 would hash wrongly. The CSV import sends blobs as base64 in the JSON command and infra/pocketbase/pb_hooks/catalog_lib.js decodes and hashes them in pure JS before $filesystem.fileFromBytes, so blobs are checked and written in the same transaction; tooling/catalog-import test the_route_hashes_blob_bytes_exactly checks it against Rust's sha2 at 1, 55, 56, 63, 64, 119, 120 and 300,000 bytes (PocketBase cannot store an empty file, so the route refuses empty blobs, and it refuses a blob that no CAD item revision in the request uses). Canonical documents whose SHA-256 is their identity (revision snapshots) are stored in text fields with an explicit max (a TextField max of 0 means 5000), never json fields, so the hashed bytes round-trip. Shared hook code lives in a non-.pb.js file loaded with require(`${__hooks}/catalog_lib.js`) inside the handler.

title: Derive Catalog record IDs from content and compare CSV imports with stored state on the server
rationale: Every Catalog record ID is the first 15 hex digits of SHA-256('kicad-parts:<kind>:v1\n<key>') (part from IPN, CAD item from kind + LIB:NAME, CAD item revision from CAD item + revision number (since kicad-parts-54d5; see the pattern 'CAD item revisions are numbered; snapshots name them by number and hash'), blob from its bytes' hash, Change and audit entry from the correlation ID), computed in crates/catalog/src/ids.rs and re-derived by the route, so re-imports find the same records without a mapping table; a stored record is reused only if its hash or key matches, otherwise 409 id_collision. A symbol's blob is the exact bytes of that one top-level symbol (its source keeps file path, file hash and byte range), so editing a neighbouring symbol does not revise it; footprints and 3D models are whole files. Manufacturer parts (main first) are part details, so adding, removing or reordering one saves new part details (no revision, since kicad-parts-7556); a part has one datasheet, and a substitutes.csv datasheet that is neither blank nor the part's is a substitutes-csv-datasheet-differs import problem. POST /api/catalog/csv-imports compares with stored state in one transaction, and a Change is made only when there is at least one new revision or saved part details. Which import changes are saved and which become import problems is in the pattern 'Part details are stored apart from part revisions'. Supplier part numbers, LCSC codes and prices stay in the source, never in part details or a revision. Replaced in part: when a run is recorded without a Change and when an import is a 422 noop are now in mx-c5e787; expected revisions and the checkout check are in mx-64c42a.

name: Catalog write guards and tamper tests
description: catalog_write_guards.pb.js refuses every create, update and delete of catalog_* records through the record API with 403, superusers included (onRecord*Request hooks), and every update or delete from server code (onRecordUpdate/onRecordDelete) except moving a part's current_revision, or its current_details, to the one saved right after it (same part, number+1, predecessor = old current). New catalog_part_details must be the part's newest number + 1, with the newest as predecessor and the ID derived from part and number (onRecordCreate). A new CAD item revision must be its CAD item's newest number + 1, with the newest as predecessor and the ID derived from CAD item and number (onRecordCreate). Collection drops in down migrations are not record deletes, so rollback still works. Tests that need a tampered record (ID-collision cases) stop the server, UPDATE data.db with rusqlite, and restart on the same data dir.

title: Each CSV import run records what the CSV said; the zero-loss report rebuilds the CSV from the latest run
rationale: A CSV import run's audit entry (catalog_audit_entries: csv_file, csv_import_number from 1 without gaps, source_commit, allowed_older_checkout, file_hashes, sources) records the files read with byte hashes, each CSV file's header line and every row's bytes, the current revision and details it left each part at (parts: [{ipn, revision, details}]), the parts earlier runs made that no row makes now (removed_parts), and the IDs of every import problem it found (new or already stored), whether or not it makes a Change. Every run sends exactly one catalog-csv source (database/<csvFile>.csv) and one substitutes-csv source; the route checks sha256(header + rows) against the file hash, refuses empty rows, and checks that every part's source row is one of those rows. A run is recorded (200 nothing_changed) whenever it read other files than the previous run of the same CSV file, even with no revision or problem, so the latest run always holds what the CSV says now; 422 noop only when nothing is new and the files are the same. A part an earlier run made that no row makes now gets a part-not-in-csv-file import problem whose detail does not name a run, so every later run finds it again; nothing is deleted. tooling/catalog-import zero_loss.rs rebuilds the CSV from the latest run (checking the recorded row count against the parsed rows, and file_hashes against the recorded files), matches rows by IPN (row problems by row number plus exact row bytes), accepts only import problems the latest run found (problems are shared by content, so an earlier run's problem must never explain a row) and none for two rows, compares each row's Symbol and Footprint with the revision, and every other details column with the part details, that run left the part at (so later edits do not matter; a kind kept by csv-details-differ-from-edited-details or csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision is accounted as an import problem), reads supplier data from the run's rows, and matches incomplete-main-manufacturer-part problems by the row's own MPN and Manufacturer. A symbol keeps its revision when a neighbouring symbol in its library changes, so its stored source may name an older file hash and byte range: the report checks the blob against the whole symbol in the current file, and when the source names the current file it also checks the stored range. It checks 3D model references on the footprint revision the parts actually bind. Current revision sources are never used by the report.

title: CSV imports carry the current revision they expect per part, and the importer refuses an older checkout
rationale: ImportCommand carries the current revision and current details it expects per part (parts[].expectedRevision and parts[].expectedDetails, 0 for a part expected to be new; kicad-parts-7556) and per CAD item (cadItemRevisions[].expectedRevision, read by read_import_state; a moved CAD item is a 409 conflict listed in cadItemConflicts) and the latest import run of its CSV file it read (expectedCsvImport, 0 if none); both are set only by ImportCommand::expecting(read_import_state), and the older-checkout setting only by allowing_older_checkout. These fields are private because each setter derives the correlation ID again from the import fingerprint plus all three, so re-running the same import after it applied gets a fresh comparison (422 noop) and re-sending an identical command replays. The same import with a different reason still gets 409 correlation_reused, as any reused ID for a different request does. If another import of the file landed in between, POST /api/catalog/csv-imports answers 409 newer_import_run; if any part's current revision or details differ, 409 conflict listing every such part with its current revision and details (the message names at most 10). Both write nothing and are not stored, like edit conflicts. read_import_state downloads only small fields (the fields= query; audit entries carry file_hashes, JSON [[path, sha]], for this). The server cannot run git, so tooling/catalog-import checkout.rs (used by services::prepare_import) checks the latest import run of every CSV file. If it came from a clean commit X, the import must be X or a descendant (git merge-base --is-ancestor; an import at Y+dirty counts as Y). If it came from X+dirty, the import must still be X or a descendant, and every file BOTH imports read (such as substitutes.csv or a shared symbol library; another CSV file does not count) must have the hash that run recorded or, for a descendant Y, must have changed in git between X and Y (git --literal-pathspecs diff --quiet X Y -- path), so a commit of the change still imports but a clean checkout, an unrelated later commit or other local changes cannot undo it. services::read_source_commit tells a missing git apart from a folder outside git, so the check says plainly when git is not installed. A commit the checkout lacks, files not read from git and recorded commits that are not 40 hex digits are refused too, one line per commit. allow_older_checkout skips the check and is recorded as allowed_older_checkout on the run's audit entry.

name: Blob hashing in the CSV import route: UTF-8 text through PocketBase, other bytes through JavaScript
description: $security.sha256 hashes text only. A blob whose bytes are UTF-8 (every real CAD file so far) is sent as text (blobs[].text) and the route hashes it with $security.sha256(text) and stores toBytes(text): both turn the same JS string into the same UTF-8 bytes, so the stored bytes are exactly the hashed ones (about 50 ms per MiB; invalid UTF-8 or lone surrogates become U+FFFD on both sides, so a false hash claim is refused). Other bytes are sent as base64 and decoded and hashed in pure JS (catalog_lib.js, about 3 s per MiB; the 60 s client timeout would fail near 20 MiB). Exactly one of text/base64 per blob. Passing a Go []byte or a JS array to $security.sha256 does NOT hash the bytes: goja stringifies it as '72,69,...'. The route sets $apis.bodyLimit(32 MiB) (PocketBase's default; above it PocketBase answers 413 or resets the connection while the client still sends), and submit_import serializes the body once and refuses one over IMPORT_BODY_LIMIT before sending. Measured on the real catalog: g-con (largest model, 1.5 MiB) 5.4 s -> 0.17 s; the 7 CSV files using all 13 models 14.4 s -> 0.67 s; largest request g-con at 1,900,969 bytes (1.8 MiB). An empty 3D model file is an empty-3d-model-reference import problem (file kept as a source), never a blob; the route still refuses empty blobs. Tests: tooling/catalog-import tests the_route_hashes_blob_bytes_exactly (both forms) and pocketbase_categories every_real_3d_model_imports_in_one_request_per_csv_file.

name: Catalog hook storage and shared code
description: Kept from mx-be5c16: canonical documents whose SHA-256 is their identity (revision snapshots) are stored in text fields with an explicit max (a TextField max of 0 means 5000), never json fields, so the hashed bytes round-trip. Shared hook code lives in a non-.pb.js file loaded with require(`${__hooks}/catalog_lib.js`) inside the handler; values used when registering a route (such as $apis.bodyLimit's limit) may be top-level consts of the .pb.js file.

title: Extra MPN columns, MPN TBC and unknown MPN columns become import problems; Excluded from BOM comes only from KiCad's own BOM flags
rationale: route_column: 'MPN' followed by digits (g-rfm MPN2) is ExtraMpn, 'MPN TBC' (g-rvr) is MpnToBeConfirmed, and any other header containing 'mpn' in any case ('MPN 2', 'Alt MPN', 'mpn2') is UnknownMpn; none goes into the part details. A non-blank MPN2 is an mpn-without-manufacturer import problem (detail: column, mpn, row_manufacturer) because a manufacturer part needs a manufacturer and nothing in the CSV says the row's Manufacturer makes it (Wurth 3670128 vs MS128-10F). MPN TBC is an mpn-to-be-confirmed import problem (detail: column, value): unconfirmed MPNs are not approved manufacturer parts. UnknownMpn values are unknown-mpn-column import problems (detail: column, value); no real CSV has one. Blank cells add nothing. PartRevision.excluded_from_bom (part of the revision since kicad-parts-7556; serde default, written only when true, last field; a CAD edit copies it from the current revision, so a rebinding edit keeps it and nobody can set it by hand; kicad-parts-ccc0 decides how it follows new CAD) is true when a local symbol the part binds says (in_bom no), or every footprint choice is a local footprint with exclude_from_bom in its (attr ...). If only some footprint choices are marked (an unread KiCad-library choice counts as not marked) and the symbol is not, it stays unset and a footprint-choices-disagree-on-bom import problem keeps the choices. Notes and descriptions are never read. In the CSV catalog it is set for ART-0000-0001 only (g-art:TestPoint). ART-0001-0006 has no evidence either way: its symbol g-con:Conn_PIC_TagConnect_TC2030 is missing (missing-member) and its footprint is in KiCad's bundled library, which is not read. The g-no_bom libraries are all marked but unused. The zero-loss report checks all these rules (column table in zero_loss.rs, tests every_column_of_every_csv_file_has_one_destination and the_zero_loss_report_fails_when_its_new_checks_find_a_loss) and all 21 CSV files pass the pilot.

title: Edits made in the app always win over CSV imports; differences are accepted field by field
rationale: User decision, 2026-10-10. A re-import never overwrites what an edit saved. Since kicad-parts-7556 this holds per part and per kind: a part's details follow the CSV only while its current details came from a CSV import, and its CAD only while its current revision did; otherwise csv-details-differ-from-edited-details or csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision keeps the row (catalog_csv_imports.pb.js). So a description edited in the app stays while a CSV footprint change still adds a revision. The desktop app shows that import problem on the part; the person can open it, see each field where the CSV differs, and pick which CSV values to accept, which saves a normal edit. Unpicked fields stay as they are.

title: Number CAD item revisions like parts; KiCad always gets the current revision
rationale: User decision on 9e05, 2026-10-10 (option 1). Going back to earlier content adds a new numbered CAD item revision, while the bytes stay stored once, so a CAD item's current revision is always its newest. KiCad has no revision concept (database libraries refer to Library:Name); how KiCad gets revisions is now mx-f75a28. Built in kicad-parts-54d5: a CAD item revision ID is deriveId('cad-item-revision', cad_item + newline + number); part revisions (part details before kicad-parts-7556) and footprint snapshots name a revision by cad_item, number and snapshot_sha256. A binding (a part's symbol or footprint, or a footprint's 3D model) keeps the revision it names while its CAD content is the same, because the same content under a newer number is not a change (mx-5e5fb1). Only a change of CAD content, or a Symbol or Footprint field naming another CAD item, moves a binding, and then it names the CAD item's current revision. So parts the imports keep follow A, B, A to revisions 1, 2 and 3, while a part that missed B (its CAD kept by an edit, or in another CSV file) stays on revision 1 with no new revision and no import problem. Edits never renumber a binding (restores, which copied an older revision exactly, were removed in kicad-parts-9296). Parts do not always bind a CAD item's current number. How it works: the pattern 'CAD item revisions are numbered; snapshots name them by number and hash' (mx-0a590f).

title: Imports from uncommitted changes are refused unless overridden
rationale: User decision on 7348, 2026-10-10: commit first, because one simple rule is easier to explain than tracking uncommitted changes across later imports. Not built yet; mx-64c42a describes the current behaviour until kicad-parts-7348 lands.

title: A revision is a CAD change; part details and manufacturer parts are shared; archive instead of restore
rationale: User decision, 2026-10-10. Old products must keep the exact parts they were designed with while new designs use the newest. A part revision is the exact symbol, footprint and 3D model revisions a part uses, and only a CAD change adds one; the same CAD content under a newer CAD item number is not a change. Part details (description, value, datasheet) and manufacturer parts belong to the IPN and every revision shares them: changing them is recorded in the history but adds no revision. A part that can no longer replace the old one gets a new IPN. Restore goes away: a bad revision is archived (hidden from KiCad and the app, still found by designs that use it, never deleted), and the current revision is the newest one not archived. The IPN never carries the revision. Built in kicad-parts-7556 (shared part details, revisions as CAD only; see the pattern 'Part details are stored apart from part revisions') after kicad-parts-9296 removed Restore; archive comes in kicad-parts-5bea.

name: CAD item revisions are numbered; snapshots name them by number and hash
description: Seed kicad-parts-54d5. IDs: a CAD item revision is deriveId('cad-item-revision', cad_item + newline + number) (crates/catalog ids.rs CadItemRevisionId::new, catalog_lib.js); blobs stay content-derived, so revisions with the same bytes share one blob. A CAD item's current revision is its newest number (no pointer field); a create guard in catalog_write_guards.pb.js refuses a new CAD item revision that is not newest+1 with the newest as predecessor and the derived ID. References: CadReferenceTarget and ModelTarget::CadItemRevision are {cad_item, number, snapshot_sha256}; the number gives the record ID, the hash lets readers (desktop checked_snapshot, zero-loss report) check the record. Same content: CadItemDetails::content_sha256 (and contentOf in catalog_csv_imports.pb.js, over key-sorted canonicalJson so key order cannot hide equal content) hashes a snapshot with its 3D model binding numbers set to 0, so a footprint naming model revision 3 has the same content as one naming model revision 1 when those models have the same content. Keeping: a binding keeps the revision it names while its content hash equals the CAD item's current revision's; otherwise it names the current revision. Import: CsvCatalog::import numbers as if the catalog were empty; ImportCommand::expecting calls CsvImport::numbered_against(read_import_state's current_cad: each CAD item's current revision with a footprint's model bindings, from cad_item_revisions fields id,cad_item,number,snapshot_sha256,snapshot, and each part's current bindings, from part revisions' cad_item_revisions relation), 3D models first. Each cadItemRevisions entry carries expectedRevision (current number read, 0 if new), number (expected if content equals the current revision's snapshot, else expected+1) and the derived id. The route refuses a wrong id or number (400), a second entry for one CAD item (400), a binding with keys other than kind/cad_item/number/snapshot_sha256 (400), a new CAD item revision whose content equals the current revision's and differs only in the numbers it names (400), a binding that does not keep exactly the revision the part's (or footprint's) stored current revision binds while that has the same content as the CAD item's current revision after the request (400, so the server requires keeping, not just allows it), and any other binding that is not that current revision (400); 409 conflict with cadItemConflicts [{kind,key,expectedRevision,currentRevision}] when a CAD item moved since it was read. A stored current revision whose ID, number or snapshot hash is inconsistent is an id_collision. A part whose current revision an edit saved, and whose CAD content really differs in the row, gets csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision ('the symbols, footprints or 3D models that the row of X uses differ from its current revision N, which was saved by an edit'; kicad-parts-7556). Edits keep a binding the current revision already has exactly; a newly named reference binds the current revision. (Restores, which copied the stored bytes, were removed in kicad-parts-9296.) The zero-loss report compares the parts' bindings of one reference by content hash and checks every bound revision. Migration 1791700000_cad_item_revision_numbers.js drops the unique (cad_item, snapshot_sha256) index (adds a plain one) and refuses to start, changing nothing, on data whose CAD item revision IDs are not number-derived; its undo refuses whenever any CAD item revision exists. Tests: crates/catalog csv_import going_back_to_earlier_cad_content_is_numbered_as_a_new_revision; tooling/catalog-import pocketbase_reimports going_back_to_earlier_cad_content_adds_a_revision_that_parts_bind, pocketbase_import (forged ids/numbers, stale CAD items, old data and undo refused), pocketbase_edits server_code_cannot_move_a_part_backwards_or_skip_a_revision, desktop_team_previews after_going_back_to_earlier_content_previews_draw_each_revisions_own_cad.

title: Archive rules: never the last revision, undo with a reason, part revisions only; per-part ownership of details and CAD
rationale: User decisions, 2026-10-10 (bd76 plan, all recommendations approved). The last revision of a part that is not archived cannot be archived (add a corrected revision first), so every part always has a current revision. Archiving can be undone (Unarchive) with a reason, by the same people who can archive. Only part revisions are archived for now; CAD item revisions keep current = newest. App edits win over CSV imports per part and per kind: a part follows CSV details only while its latest saved details came from an import, and CSV CAD only while its current revision came from an import; otherwise the difference is an import problem to accept field by field (kicad-parts-75a5). Excluded from BOM is recalculated from the CAD of every new revision and shown read-only (kicad-parts-ccc0). The app may edit Value and change Symbol and Footprint, with the hint that a part with a different value, package or pinout needs a new IPN. Sim_* columns are shared part details. Not built yet (kicad-parts-bd76 steps).

name: Part details are stored apart from part revisions
description: Seed kicad-parts-7556 (decision mx-5e5fb1). Two kinds of immutable, numbered, hashed records per part. catalog_part_details (migration 1791800000_shared_part_details.js): part, number from 1 per part, predecessor, change, snapshot (PartDetails schema kicad-parts/part-details/2: ipn, fields, manufacturer_parts; never Symbol or Footprint), snapshot_sha256, source; ID deriveId('part-details', part + newline + number). catalog_part_revisions keep their collection, but the snapshot is PartRevision schema kicad-parts/part-revision/1: ipn, cad_fields (Symbol and Footprint exactly as written), cad_references, excluded_from_bom. catalog_parts gains current_details and current_details_number; guards let both pointers move only to the next one, and new part details must be newest+1 with the derived ID. Change kinds are csv-import and edit; a Change holds at least one part revision, CAD item revision or saved part details. Edits (POST /api/catalog/edits, catalog_lib.js publishEdit): { correlationId, reason, ipn, details?: { expectedDetails, fields, manufacturerParts }, cad?: { expectedRevision, fields } }, each section sent only when it changed (catalog-browser compares with the details and revision the person started from), each checked against its own number, so a details edit never conflicts with a CAD change; 409 gives currentDetails and/or currentRevision for what moved; applied gives details and/or revision. CSV imports: route_column sends Symbol and Footprint to ColumnRoute::Cad; parts[] carry expectedRevision, expectedDetails, details { snapshot, snapshotSha256 }, revision { snapshot, snapshotSha256 } and one source. Ownership is per part and per kind: changed details are saved only if the current details' Change kind is csv-import, else csv-details-differ-from-edited-details; changed CAD adds a revision only if the current revision's is, else csv-cad-differs-from-edited-revision. When both are unchanged the row is compared with the source of whichever current record was saved later: part-last-saved-without-csv-source if that was an edit, csv-row-changed-without-part-details-change if only supplier data changed. Runs record parts as {ipn, revision, details}; Counts add partDetails and updatedDetails. The replica holds each part's current revision and current details (a Change may hold only details); the desktop history has one entry per Change (HistoryEntry with revision and/or details). The migration refuses old data (any part revision) with a plain start-fresh message; its undo refuses any saved part details, so a full rollback works only on a catalog without parts.
